Deputy

DATE: September 30, 2026         CLOSING DATE: UNTIL FILLED

 

POSITION: Deputy

 

DEPARTMENT: ACSO

 

Responsibilities:

Under general supervision, exercises responsibilities for the enforcement of state and local laws relating to public safety and welfare. Reports to assigned Sergeant, Staff Sergeant, or Lieutenant.

 

Required Licenses or Certifications:

                                                                Must possess, or be able to obtain by time of hire, a valid Driver’s License without a record of suspension or revocation in any state.

  • Working knowledge of local, state, and federal laws on law enforcement.
  • Working knowledge of law enforcement guidelines and criminal investigation methods and techniques.
  • Working knowledge of court procedures.
  • Skill in the use and care of firearms and other law enforcement-related equipment.
  • Skill in administering first aid.
  • Ability to safely operate a motor vehicle and other assigned equipment.
  • Ability to act quickly and correctly in emergencies.
  • Ability to pay close attention to detail.
  • Ability to enforce the law courteously, tactfully, firmly, and impartially.
  • Ability to handle confidential information.
  • Ability to communicate effectively both orally and in writing.
  • Ability to use a computer and related software.
  • Ability to meet specific physical requirements.

 

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

 Formal Education and Experience

6 months+ training beyond High School Up to 3-years experience

Posted 1 Month Ago full-time
Detention Control and Property Specialist

DATE :    September 1, 2026                                                  CLOSING DATE:  Until Filled

 

POSITION:     Detention Control and Property Specialist

 STARTING PAY:  $37,385 up to $42,409

DEPARTMENT:   ACSO/ Detention Center

 

Responsibilities:

Performs responsible civilian detention support work involving the operation of detention center control rooms, electronic security systems, surveillance equipment, inmate property intake and release, and related detention support functions. Employees in this position are responsible for monitoring facility security systems, controlling inmate movement through electronic access systems, maintaining accurate records, and safeguarding inmate property in accordance with established policies and procedures. Work is performed under the supervision of a Detention Corporal, Sergeant, Lieutenant, or other designated supervisor.

 

Required Licenses, Skills, or Certifications:

Must possess and maintain a valid Driver’s License.

Must successfully complete all detention center training required for civilian detention support personnel.

Must be capable of obtaining and maintaining access to criminal justice information systems (CJIS) as required.

Must successfully pass all required background investigations and security clearances.

 

Physical Requirements:

Ability to sit, stand, walk, and perform assigned duties for extended periods.

Ability to observe multiple video monitors and read computer screens for prolonged periods.

Ability to hear and communicate effectively through radios, telephones, and intercom systems.

Ability to lift and carry inmate property and other materials weighing up to 30 pounds.

Ability to respond quickly to emergency situations within the facility when required.

Ability to maintain alertness and concentration during extended shifts.

 

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

Formal Education and Experience:

High school diploma or GED required.

Previous experience in security monitoring, dispatching, corrections support, customer service, records management, property control, communications, administrative support, or a related field preferred.

Experience operating computerized systems and maintaining detailed records preferred.

Equivalent combinations of education, training, and experience may be considered.

 

 

Complete an application located on the website  https://www.andersonsheriff.org/employment

 

Submitting Your Application:

All required documents must be copied before submitting your application. You will be required to upload the documents during your submission.  If you do not follow the instructions or are unable to submit said documents, you will need to save a draft and come back to it when you are able to submit all required documents, images or contacts.  

Applications must be completed digitally. Handwritten applications will not be accepted.

recruiting@andersonsheriff.com

Posted 1 Month Ago full-time
Stormwater Inspector

DATE :    August 19, 2026                                                  CLOSING DATE:  Until Filled

 

POSITION:     STORMWATER INSPECTOR

 

DEPARTMENT:   STORMWATER

 

Responsibilities:

Performs a variety of routine and complex technical work in the evaluation of stormwater management controls at construction sites, developed sites, and county facilities. Assists with the implementation of the County’s stormwater program.

 

 

Competencies for Successful Performance of Job Duties:

  • Thorough knowledge of sediment and erosion control inspection practices; ability to read and understand complicated plans and blueprints; knowledge of federal and state stormwater regulations and permits.
  • Ability to conduct GIS data collection and use ArcGIS software; thorough knowledge of Windows and Microsoft Office software; knowledge of water sample collection and analysis methods.
  • Ability to establish effective working relationships with contractors, developers, architects, engineers, owners, and the public; Ability to communicate effectively orally and in writing.

 

 

Required Licenses, Skills, or Certifications:

  • A valid driver’s license or ability to obtain one.
  • Must have SCDES Certified Erosion Prevention & Sediment Control Inspector Certification or be able to obtain the certification within six (6) months of hire date.
  • Must have FAA Unmanned Aerial Systems Remote Pilot Certification or be able to obtain the certification within six (6) months of hire date.

 

 

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

Formal Education and Experience:

  • Bachelor’s Degree in biological sciences, construction science, environmental science, natural resources, environmental engineering, civil engineering, or related field
  • 1 to 3 years’ experience

Posted 2 Months Ago full-time
Paramedic

DATE:            July 31, 2026                                   CLOSING DATE: UNTIL FILLED

 

POSITION:           Paramedic        

 

DEPARTMENT:   Emergency Medical Services    

 

Responsibilities:

The fundamental responsibility of the Paramedic is to preserve life, alleviate suffering, promote health, to do no harm, and to encourage the quality and equal availability of emergency medical care.

 

The Paramedic is qualified in advanced prehospital emergency care and services by a competency-based educational program of clinical, didactic, and practice emergency vehicle operator as well as provide of prehospital advanced life support (ALS). The standard of practice of the Paramedic shall be in accordance with the most current edition of the US DOT “Emergency Medical Technician-Paramedic: National Standard Curriculum”, as modified by the South Carolina Department of Health and Environmental Control, Bureau of EMS, and Anderson County Emergency Medical Services.

 

The Anderson County EMS Paramedic is primarily responsible for responding to 911 requests for service via a Quick Response Vehicle (QRV), providing medical assessment of the patient, initiating advanced life support care when required, and attending to the patient during transport which is provided by a contracted ambulance provider when needed.

 

Required Education and Experience:

  • High School Diploma or Equivalency
  • 1 to 3 years’ experience

 

Required Licenses or Certification:

  • Current South Carolina State Driver’s License
  • Current South Carolina State and/or National Registered Certification as Paramedic
  • Current Basic Cardiac Life Support Certification (BCLS)
  • Current Advanced Cardiac Life Support Certification (ACLS)
  • Current Pediatric Advanced Life Certification (PALS)- May be obtained upon employment

Paramedic
Posted 2 Months Ago full-time
Paramedic

DATE:            July 31, 2026                                   CLOSING DATE: UNTIL FILLED

 

POSITION:           Paramedic        

 

DEPARTMENT:   Emergency Medical Services    

 

Responsibilities:

The fundamental responsibility of the Paramedic is to preserve life, alleviate suffering, promote health, to do no harm, and to encourage the quality and equal availability of emergency medical care.

 

The Paramedic is qualified in advanced prehospital emergency care and services by a competency-based educational program of clinical, didactic, and practice emergency vehicle operator as well as provide of prehospital advanced life support (ALS). The standard of practice of the Paramedic shall be in accordance with the most current edition of the US DOT “Emergency Medical Technician-Paramedic: National Standard Curriculum”, as modified by the South Carolina Department of Health and Environmental Control, Bureau of EMS, and Anderson County Emergency Medical Services.

 

The Anderson County EMS Paramedic is primarily responsible for responding to 911 requests for service via a Quick Response Vehicle (QRV), providing medical assessment of the patient, initiating advanced life support care when required, and attending to the patient during transport which is provided by a contracted ambulance provider when needed.

 

Required Education and Experience:

  • High School Diploma or Equivalency
  • 1 to 3 years’ experience

 

Required Licenses or Certification:

  • Current South Carolina State Driver’s License
  • Current South Carolina State and/or National Registered Certification as Paramedic
  • Current Basic Cardiac Life Support Certification (BCLS)
  • Current Advanced Cardiac Life Support Certification (ACLS)
  • Current Pediatric Advanced Life Certification (PALS)- May be obtained upon employment

POSITION:         Equipment Operator

DEPARTMENT:  SOLID WASTE

 

General Summary:

Operates and maintains a variety of light and heavy motor equipment used in the collection, transporting and disposal of Solid Waste at a designated landfill.

 

 Competencies for Successful Performance of Job Duties:

  • Working knowledge of material recovery facility, landfill operations, convenience center operations and a working knowledge of safety operations.
  • Skill in operation of listed tools and equipment. Heavy equipment such as Bulldozer, Compactor, Front-end loader, and Tri-axle, and Roll-Off trucks, Off-Road Truck; mechanical equipment; riding mower, air tank, push mower, and sprayers, other motorized vehicles and equipment: high production, high-density baler, sorting line.
  • Ability to accurately screen in-coming wastes; ability to establish effective working relationships with other employees, supervisors, and regulatory agencies.
  • Must possess working knowledge of department terminology; working knowledge of sanitary landfill operations and requirements; working knowledge of safety operations. Skill in operating the necessary landfill equipment. Ability to accurately compile and portray complex data; ability to establish an effective working relationship with other employees, supervisors, and regulatory agencies.
  • Ability to understand and follow oral or written instructions; ability to observe proper safety precautions; ability to establish effective working relationships with other employees, supervisors, and the public; ability to perform heavy manual tasks under varying weather conditions and the ability to drive and operate a variety of light and heavy equipment under varying conditions.

 

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

Required Education and Experience

  • High School diploma or equivalency
  • 1 to 3 years’ experience

Required Licenses, Skills or Certifications

  • A valid Driver’s or ability to obtain one and CDL/ Class B License, if requested.
